parallel.requirements: Recognized clean-room reverse engineering of ditaa from bundled docs and executable observations only, with no source search, no wrapper, and an executable-equivalent deliverable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent selected Java/Java2D for fidelity, kept implementation responsibility, then launched an 11-area workflow plus two direct investigation subagents for hard details.
parallel.implementation: Created helper tools, behavior probes, `build/Boot.java`, and `src/ditaa/Cell.java`; no complete executable or buildable full reimplementation is evidenced.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Final artifact contained notes, tools, corpus, Boot.java, and Cell.java but no assembled compileable replacement; final response file was empty.
parallel.verification: Performed many local SVG/PNG/CLI probes and compiler API tests, but no final integrated build/evaluator-aligned acceptance after implementation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Agent timed out; workflow was killed with result null; several children were interrupted or errored; official evaluation completed with compile_failed and 681 tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room ditaa reimplementation constraints and used bundled README/docs plus executable behavior as the information source.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single actor performed sequential exploration without delegation; no subagent or workflow ownership boundaries existed.
serial.implementation: Focused on probes for CLI, SVG, PNG, geometry, arrows, line handling, round corners, and text metrics; no implementation source was written into the submitted workspace.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Submitted artifact retained the original documentation/repository/executable context but no new replacement implementation source or assembled deliverable.
serial.verification: Ran many observation commands and measurements, but there was no final implemented binary to build or verify.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Agent timed out during local text/font experiments; official evaluation completed with compile_failed and 681 tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the clean-room ditaa reimplementation task, the no-source/no-wrapper restrictions, CLI/SVG/PNG behavior, and the need for an executable replacement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same ditaa clean-room task and used README plus executable observations to probe CLI, SVG, PNG, geometry, and text behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The recognized requirements were materially similar; the difference was not a misunderstanding of the prompt but how much deliverable work each attempt reached before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent kept implementation ownership but decomposed research into an 11-area workflow and later two direct subagents for vertex ordering and text metrics.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had one actor and no delegation; all exploration remained in a single local timeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created broad concurrent research ownership while serial stayed sequential; the parent still owned implementation, so this is not a missing-owner episode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow brief supplied detailed shared facts, scratch-space rules, note/corpus deliverables, and feature-area assignments for child explorers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor carried all discovered facts locally without inter-agent handoffs or interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained context label is supported: the problem was not a known requirement omitted from a child brief or an incompatible cross-agent contract, but the unresolved breadth and killed workflow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel selected a Java/Java2D path, verified compiler API availability, wrote `build/Boot.java` and `src/ditaa/Cell.java`, but did not finish a compileable executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial explored behavior deeply but did not write implementation source into the workspace before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached partial source creation while serial remained entirely observational; both nevertheless failed at compile time.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The background workflow was launched and left to run; its state later had `result:null`, killed status, child errors, and multiple in-progress children, while direct subagents were killed at the end.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; the serial trajectory ends with local probing and timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unreturned child/workflow work, but that lifecycle symptom is part of the broader fan-out budget episode rather than an independent completed-result join failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children were instructed to write notes and corpus files; the final artifact included notes/tools/corpus plus two Java files, with no proven collision or overwrite among live agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not create concurrent shared-state writes and its artifact consisted of the original repository/documentation files rather than a submitted implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared research outputs but no evidence of a concrete write collision; integration simply never reached a finished assembled implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed many behavioral probes and some Java harness checks, but no final integrated build/test or evaluator-aligned acceptance occurred before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed many black-box probes of CLI, geometry, lines, text, and fonts, but no final implementation verification occurred because there was no implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on exploratory probes; neither closed with an integrated acceptance test for a delivered replacement executable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 22 subagents, 526 workflow-child tool calls, and 1.45M workflow-child tokens; the workflow state shows killed status after retries/errors and the agent timed out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used only Bash calls, no delegation, and also timed out after continuing local experiments.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the wall-clock budget, but parallel spent a distinct large budget slice on broad concurrent exploration that displaced completion of the Java deliverable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current official evaluations completed and failed with compile_failed, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome. Parallel differs concretely because it began a Java skeleton but spent a large budget slice on a killed multi-child exploration workflow; serial stayed single-actor and never produced source. The retained pattern is therefore an adverse parallel process difference, not an explanation for a different official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Broad 11-area workflow plus retries/errors consumed time and tokens before implementation/assembly finished.
Parent launched additional direct subagents late and did not reach a final build/test handoff.
Artifact contained only partial Java source plus research files and failed to compile.
serial_contributors: Serial control used no delegation and remained in local probing.
Serial did not create implementation source before timeout, so it also failed compile.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial failure is chiefly ordinary non-completion of implementation under timeout.
Parallel had partial Java implementation files whereas serial had none, but both lacked a compileable delivered executable.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both-fail comparison; retained pattern is a supported parallel adverse process contributor, not an outcome-differential root cause
